short: ISO/IEC 27701 is the ISO and IEC requirements standard for a privacy information management system; the current edition, ISO/IEC 27701:2025, specifies PIMS requirements in its own right rather than as an extension of ISO/IEC 27001, and it is a certifiable management system standard.
title: ISO/IEC 27701, Privacy Information Management Systems
subtitle: The ISO/IEC requirements standard for a privacy information management system (PIMS)
body_html:
What ISO/IEC 27701 is

ISO/IEC 27701 is the ISO and IEC standard for a privacy information management system (PIMS). It is owned by committee ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27. The current edition is ISO/IEC 27701:2025, the second edition, published on 14 October 2025. It replaces ISO/IEC 27701:2019, which ISO lists as withdrawn.

The two editions are framed differently. ISO described the 2019 edition as an extension to ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27002, applicable to organisations processing PII within an information security management system. ISO's scope for the 2025 edition says it specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving a PIMS, with guidance on implementing them. The 2025 title and scope no longer describe it as an extension of ISO/IEC 27001.

What it covers

  • Requirements for a privacy information management system: establishing it, implementing it, maintaining it and improving it over time.
  • Guidance to help implement those requirements.
  • Organisations that are PII controllers, PII processors, or both, and hold responsibility and accountability for processing PII.
  • Organisations of every type and size, including companies, government bodies and not-for-profits.

How a claim is made and checked

ISO/IEC 27701 contains requirements, so an organisation can be audited and certified against it.

ISO/IEC 17021-1 describes management system certification as a third-party conformity assessment activity carried out by certification bodies. For privacy management systems, ISO published ISO/IEC 27706:2025 on the same day as ISO/IEC 27701:2025. It sets requirements for bodies that audit and certify a PIMS according to ISO/IEC 27701, in addition to ISO/IEC 17021-1, and can serve as a criteria document for accrediting those bodies.

It replaced ISO/IEC TS 27006-2:2021, whose scope covered certification of a PIMS according to ISO/IEC 27701 in combination with ISO/IEC 27001. The 2025 certification-body standard drops that combination wording. Read together, ISO's records describe a PIMS that is certified against ISO/IEC 27701 itself, where the 2019 arrangement certified it as an addition to an ISO/IEC 27001 system.

What a claim does not mean

  • It is a management system certificate. It shows that a privacy management system was audited within a stated scope, not that every processing activity is lawful.
  • It is not a certificate of compliance with GDPR or any other data protection law.
  • A certificate to the 2019 edition was issued as an extension to an ISO/IEC 27001 system. Check which edition a certificate names, because the two are structured differently.
  • Any certificate has a scope, an issuing body and an expiry.

ISO/IEC 27701 in data centers

For a data center operator, the personal data in scope is often the operator's own: customer contacts, visitor and access records, CCTV, staff data. Where the operator also runs hosted or managed services, it may act as a PII processor for customers. When an operator publishes an ISO/IEC 27701 certificate, check:

  • The scope statement: which sites, which services, and whether the organisation is certified as a PII controller, a processor, or both.
  • The edition, 2019 or 2025, and for a 2019 certificate, the linked ISO/IEC 27001 certificate.
  • The certificate number, certifying body, accreditation body, issue date and expiry.

Related standards

ISO/IEC 27701 is most often seen next to ISO/IEC 27001. For cloud-specific guidance see ISO/IEC 27017 and ISO/IEC 27018. All are listed in the standards hub.
